_meta.title: P-PIV configuration: single-valued fuzzy plithogenic set + MEREC weights + PIV ranking
_meta.scope: Plithogenic PIV (P-PIV), single-valued fuzzy. NOT neutrosophic.
_meta.tags: [S] = from an original paper; [D] = team design choice. Equation/table numbers are UNVERIFIED because no PDF was attached when this file was written.
_meta.reading_rule: Keys starting with '_' are documentation and are ignored by the code.

paths._note: Relative paths resolve against the folder holding this file. --input on the CLI overrides input_csv.

columns._note: Role map used by audit_columns. Every CSV column must appear here, as a source, as a derived feature, or under one of these keys. [D]

excluded.Established_Year: [D] Age is not a quality direction (older is not demonstrably better); kept out of the ranking.
excluded.Total_Faculty: [D] Absolute size is not a quality direction; Students_Per_Faculty is the ratio actually used.
excluded.Student_Enrollment: [D] Absolute size is not a quality direction; Students_Per_Faculty is the ratio actually used.
excluded.Engineering_Courses: [D] Free-text list; Engineering_Course_Count already summarises it.
excluded.Positive_Review_Count: [D] Already summarised by Review_Sentiment_Score; avoids double counting.
excluded.Negative_Review_Count: [D] Already summarised by Review_Sentiment_Score; avoids double counting.
excluded.Neutral_Review_Count: [D] Already summarised by Review_Sentiment_Score; avoids double counting.

derived.name: Facility_Count
derived._note: [D] Number of non-empty items in the delimited Facilities text.

shrinkage._note: [D] x__adj = conf*x + (1-conf)*mean(x over ALL rows). Original columns are kept. Sources with use_adjusted=true are read from the __adj column by P-PIV.

scale_inspection._note: [D] Printed at prepare() time. A value outside [expected_min, expected_max] raises ValueError.

missing_values._note: Imputation happens ONLY for columns listed here. Any other NaN in a source column raises an error. Rows are never dropped. Example entry: "Public_Rating": {"method": "median"}

quality_flags._note: [D] Row-level flags joined with ';' in the 'column' below. ops: contains | startswith | lt | gt. Text ops are case-sensitive. A NaN cell never fires. Imputed cells add 'imputed:<column>' when flag_imputed is true.

plithogenic._note: (P, a, V, d, c) [S: structure per Smarandache 2018; equation numbers UNVERIFIED]. The attribute name, value set, dominant value and the mapping of data columns to values are [D]. Truth_T / Indeterminacy_I / Falsity_F are display-only and are never used here.

values.name: Affordability
values._caveat: Fee period (annual / first-year / total) is NOT stated in the source file; fees are third-party and unverified. Interpret this value with care.

appurtenance._note: [D] r = clip((x'-lo)/(hi-lo),0,1) with lo/hi the percentiles of the transformed source on the FULL dataset, fitted once by Member 2 and saved to frozen_params.json. degree = r (direction +1) or 1-r (direction -1).

contradiction._note: [S: axioms c(v,v)=0, symmetric, values in [0,1]] [D: estimation method]. For v != dominant, c = (1-rho)/2 where rho = Spearman between per-alternative mean source-degree of the dominant value and of v, on the full data. NaN rho must raise. Fitted once, frozen, user-overridable at runtime.

aggregation._note: [S: two-assessment intersection/union formulas; equation numbers UNVERIFIED] [D: treating the two data sources of a value as the paper's two experts; choice of operator]. One source: degree unchanged. More than max_sources_per_value: rejected unless allow_nary_extension is true AND nary_label is '[D]'.

floor._note: [D] M_ij = max(a_ij, epsilon). Needed because MEREC requires x > 0. Unfloored degrees are kept for display.

weights._note: [S: MEREC, equation numbers UNVERIFIED]. m = number of criteria. Weights are recomputed on the filtered subset by default; appurtenance anchors and contradiction stay frozen.

piv._note: [S: PIV] 'vector' normalisation is the paper default; 'none' is a [D] sensitivity option. tie_decimals [D]: scores are rounded to this many decimals before ranking so that floating-point noise (~1e-16) cannot split mathematically equal scores.

baseline._note: [D] Classical baseline: every source column as a separate criterion on RAW values (no __adj, no plithogenic grouping), with its own direction. MEREC on raw positive values, then PIV.

validation._note: [D] All settings used by validation.py. Reversal: each iteration drops drop_fraction of the rows, then compares pairwise order with the full ranking on up to max_pairs sampled pairs. Sensitivity grids: each entry is a set of dotted config paths overridden TOGETHER. The special key 'contradiction.uniform' means: method=expert with every off-diagonal c equal to that number and a zero diagonal (built from the value names). The grid ranges are [D], not published.

api._note: [D] Presentation-only settings read by main.py and the dashboard. Nothing here enters the ranking. Optional: if a key is absent the API degrades (no min-reviews filter, raw column names as labels).
api.title: Plithogenic-PIV Decision Engine

display_only_group.label: Review sentiment mix (display only, not used in ranking)

caveats: Truth_T / Indeterminacy_I / Falsity_F are shown for context only; they do not enter either ranking.
The PIV paper (Mufazzal & Muzakkir 2018) describes rank reversal as minimised, not eliminated. The Validation tab reports measured numbers on this data only.
P-PIV and classical PIV answer differently framed questions; a rank difference is a description, not evidence that either method is correct.

dummy._note: [D] Small stratified sample of the prepared frame for tests (same schema and dtypes).
